A made-up class under the real class of bonds could exist unrecorded (a lender's own bond type), and the real rule for fixed-rate bonds is not contradicted because the new class is not said to be fixed-rate.

The premise side is the kind of sentence bond news is made of (a company issues a bond).

notes: TBox expansion, paired with finance-replace-0005. Keeps the revision's relation (raises) and new conclusion (a rise in the bond's price when its yield rises) and gives it to a made-up class under the real class of bonds, so no old value is pushed out. The derived queries name invented issuers (Alderwyn Holdings, the town of Harlsden, the Port of Quillbeck) with the class stated in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops, bridge in the prompt): the inserted rule is their only route. The near unrelated query asks the real rule for fixed-rate bonds, which must stay 'it falls': a method that learned a bare 'yield up, price up' mapping would leak here. Class and issuer names are invented; the counting step records that they are absent from the corpus. Side facts and checks are those of the paired revision.
